 Glenn Close and Ralph Fiennes Decided Their Hunger Games Villains Once Had a Thing
 By Chrissy Stockton 
 Updated
 November 20, 2026 
 Glenn Close and Ralph Fiennes have a theory about their Hunger Games villains: Drusilla Sickle and President Coriolanus Snow used to be involved, and she wore him out. The actors joked about that imagined romantic history at the New York City premiere of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping on Nov. 16.
 +3 3 PHOTOS Glenn Close, Ralph Fiennes, Elle Fanning, Kieran Culkin, and fellow cast members gather at the New York City premiere of *The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping* on November 16, 2026. Photo by Mike Coppola / Getty Images. 
 Close started by asking what Snow thought of Drusilla. Fiennes took the question somewhere personal: “Do you think they’ve had a thing? They had a thing.”
 “Oh, I think so,” Close replied. “Yes, I think we definitely had a thing, and I was too old for you, and I moved on.”
 “I couldn’t keep up with you,” Fiennes said.
 +3 3 PHOTOS At the New York City premiere of *The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping* on November 16, 2026, Glenn Close, Ralph Fiennes, Elle Fanning, Kieran Culkin, Iris Apatow, and Ben Wang appeared together. Photo by Mike Coppola / Getty Images. 
 “Yes, that’s true. I tired you out,” Close added.
 That backstory comes from the actors’ playful exchange. In the movie, Close’s Drusilla escorts tributes to the Games and antagonizes District 12’s Haymitch, Maysilee, Wyatt and Louella. Joseph Zada plays the young Haymitch in a story set 24 years before the events of the original films starring Jennifer Lawrence.
 Fiennes plays Snow in middle age, between Tom Blyth’s younger version in The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes and the older president played by the late Donald Sutherland.
 Their transformations also came with very different prep times. Close said she spent more than 3 hours in makeup each day; Fiennes needed about 1 hour for makeup and a wig. “I had a full head of hair for once,” he joked.
 The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters Nov. 20.
